# Messaging

Asynchronous processing, weighted toward the simple options that are almost always sufficient.

7 unit(s). `Stages` is the maturity range where a concept applies — an agent filters on it so that concepts from a larger system than yours are not offered.

| Concept | Stages | Cost | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | --: | :-- |
| [Database-Backed Queues](database-backed-queues.md) | 1,2,3 | 0 | Using the database you already run as a job queue, which removes the dual-write problem by construction and costs no additional component. |
| [Dead-Letter Queues](dead-letter-queues.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 0 | A destination for messages that cannot be processed, which is only useful if someone is alerted and a replay procedure exists. |
| [Delivery Guarantees](delivery-guarantees.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 0 | At-most-once, at-least-once, and effectively-once — and why at-least-once plus idempotency is almost always the right choice. |
| [Idempotency](idempotency.md) | 1,2,3,4,5 | 0 | Making an operation safe to apply more than once, which is what makes retries and at-least-once delivery usable rather than dangerous. |
| [Synchronous versus Asynchronous](sync-vs-async-decision.md) | 1,2,3,4,5 | 0 | Deciding whether work belongs in the request path, based on whether the caller needs the result and whether the work can fail independently. |
| [Transactional Outbox](transactional-outbox.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 1 | Writing a message into the same transaction as the business change, then relaying it, so that a database write and a published message cannot diverge. |
| [When You Need Event Streaming](when-you-need-streaming.md) | 4,5 | 3 | The measured thresholds at which a durable, replayable event log earns its considerable operational cost — and the far more common case where it does not. |

`Cost` is the complexity points a concept adds if adopted; 0 means it is a technique rather than a component. See `frameworks/complexity-budget/`.
